summary: Gustavo Benavides works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Villanova University, attested in 1995 and 2004.
Guus Kroonen is a linguist who completed his doctoral studies under Alexander Lubotsky around 2005–2009. He held posts at the University of Copenhagen around 2013 and Leiden University in 2016.

Guy G. Stroumsa studied at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem, Harvard, and EPHE, among others. He was Lecturer, Associate Professor, and Editor at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem, and later Emeritus Professor of the Study of the Abrahamic Religions at Oxford.

Guy Newland specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, earning his PhD from the University of Virginia where he studied under Jeffrey Hopkins. He held a post as Associate Professor of Religion at Central Michigan University, attested 1996–2010.
Gyal Rong Tendzin Drakpa studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye.
Gyatsho Tshering, a Tibetologist, studied at the University of Calcutta. He founded the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives, serving as its Acting Director in 1972 and Director from 1974 to 1998.

Gyoei Fukuda studied Buddhist studies at Tendai Daigakurin around 1888–1893. He served as president (学長) of Taisho University around 1926–1944, and also held posts at Toyo University and the University of Tokyo.

Gyoei Takahashi works in Buddhist studies. He held posts as associate professor and professor at Rissho University (attested 2003–2004 and 2026), and as a staff member at the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of the Lotus Sutra (attested 2004).

Gyoko Iotani studied at Rissho University in the field of Buddhist studies. He held posts at Rissho University as associate professor, professor, and professor emeritus, and served as a former special appointed professor at Minobusan University.
Gyokusen Hosaka studied Buddhist studies at Komazawa University. He served as president (学長) of Komazawa Junior College from around 1950 to 1963.
Gyomay Kubose worked in Buddhist and religious studies, studying at Otani University and under Haya Akegarasu between around 1937 and 1941.
Gyoon Iotani studied Buddhist studies at Waseda University (attested 2015). He held a post as deputy director (副主任) at Minobusan University (attested 2026).
Gyosho Takahashi works in Buddhist studies. He held posts as professor at Minobusan Junior College (attested 1992) and Minobusan University (attested 1996).

Gyoshu Chojo is a Buddhist studies scholar. He served as a professor at Minobusan Junior College (attested 1996) and as a Faculty of Buddhist Studies professor at Minobusan University (attested 2001).
Gyula Ortutay studied at the University of Szeged from 1928 to 1934. He later held a post at Nyugat around 1935–1938.

Gyurme Dorje earned his PhD at SOAS under Philip Denwood. A Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar, he held a fellowship at the University of London / SOAS (1991–1996) and worked as a translator at the Tsadra Foundation (2007–2020).
Gyurme Pema Tekchok studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.

György Hazai was a scholar of linguistics and Iranian/Central Asian studies who studied at Eötvös Loránd University (~1950–1954). He held a post at the Institut für Orientforschung from around 1963 to 1982.

György Kara was a linguist and Central Asian specialist who studied at Eötvös Loránd University under Gyula Németh and Lajos Ligeti. He held posts at Eötvös Loránd University, the Hungarian Academy of Sciences, and Indiana University Bloomington.

Gyōin Hashimoto studied Buddhist studies and philosophy at the University of Tokyo (~1922–1925) and under Join Saeki. He served as head (管主) at Yakushiji (1939–1967) and chief abbot (管長) of Hossō-shū in 1940.
